name: Murray Gell-Mann
summary: Nobel laureate theoretical physicist known for the quark model and Eightfold Way.

name: George Zweig
summary: Physicist who proposed the ace model (constituent quarks) independently of Gell-Mann.

name: Richard Feynman
summary: Nobel laureate theoretical physicist and colleague of Gell-Mann at Caltech.

name: California Institute of Technology
summary: University in Pasadena, California where Gell-Mann and Zweig worked in the 1960s.

name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
summary: University in Cambridge, Massachusetts where Zweig was affiliated at the time of writing.

name: University of Michigan
summary: University where Zweig was an undergraduate math major.

name: Cornell University
summary: University where Hans Bethe worked, suggested to Zweig as a graduate school option.

name: Princeton University
summary: University from which Dan Kevles arrived at Caltech.

name: CERN
summary: European particle physics laboratory where Zweig visited before explaining aces to Gell-Mann.

name: Scientific American
summary: Magazine where Gell-Mann and Zweig published or attempted to publish articles.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics
summary: Prestigious award for which Feynman nominated Gell-Mann and Zweig.

name: Dan Kevles
summary: Historian of science and assistant professor at Caltech in 1964.

name: Bob Serber
summary: Physicist who discussed SU(3) representations with Gell-Mann in 1963.

name: Yuval Ne'eman
summary: Physicist who independently proposed SU(3) classification with Gell-Mann.
